title: A comparison of socioeconomic dynamics and market performance in lobster and giant freshwater prawn value chains in Sri Lanka
authors: Ruwini Basnayake and Achini De Silva
summary: Maps actors and value chains in both sectors from interviews with 748 fishers, 44 collectors and 12 exporters, and assesses margins, price spread and marketing efficiency.

title: Physicochemical and microbial characteristics of selected dried fish products in Sri Lankan markets
authors: T. M. N. P. Thennakoon, A. A. M. Subodinee, D. N. Koralagama and N. Y. Hirimuthugoda
summary: Compares moisture, protein, salt, histamine and fungal contamination in boat-dried, land-dried, imported and Maldive fish samples from Colombo and Matara markets.

title: Fishing for Life 2022: Book of abstracts
venue: South and South-East Asian Conference on Small Scale Fisheries and Aquaculture (SACSFA), ISBN 978-624-5727-24-7
summary: Keynote summaries and around 40 abstracts across resource use, policy and trade, poverty and rights, gender, and governance of small-scale fisheries.

title: Phylogenetic relationship of mangrove species found in Sri Lanka based on rbcL gene sequence
authors: N. Y. Hirimuthugoda, P. W. A. Perera, V. J. Aluthmuhandiram, A. Rashmi Ishuwara, M. M. K. Premakumara and P. K. Lal
summary: Genetically classifies Sri Lanka's 21 mangrove species, identifies Rhizophora anamalayana as a hybrid, and provides baseline data for mangrove conservation.

title: Complete mitochondrial genome of Sri Lankan Junglefowl (Gallus lafayetti) and phylogenetic study
authors: N. Y. Hirimuthugoda, A. C. Adeola, X. Chen et al.
summary: Sequences the complete mitogenome of Sri Lanka's national bird and places it within the Gallus phylogeny.

title: Status of the South Coast lobster fishery 2009
authors: U. S. P. K. Liyanage and P. Jayasinghe
venue: CENARA project report, National Aquatic Resources Research and Development Agency (NARA)
summary: Resource assessment survey of the South Coast Lobster Fisheries Management Area, Hambantota District, supported by FAO, CIDA and IFAD.

title: Mechanization ahoy! Technological change and the living standards of fishermen in southern Sri Lanka
venue: SAMUDRA Report, International Collective in Support of Fishworkers
summary: Traces state-led mechanisation of Sri Lankan fisheries since the 1930s, the credit that financed it, and its effect on fishers' incomes compared with other occupations.
